title: Domain Registrations Restore-Day Extension: Years and Amount
content:
**Pricing desk computation schedule — Domain Registrations**

Extension years ordered on the day a redemption restore is charged on a Domain Registrations domain, billed on or after 1 December 2025, are counted and priced as follows.

## A. Restore-day years

The restore-day years are the greatest whole number of years that keeps the new expiry date no more than the TLD's maximum registration term after the day of the order, the new expiry date being the expiry date recorded on the domain plus those years. They are worked out from the whole months from the day of the order to the expiry date recorded on the domain, a month counting only once its day of the month is reached: they are the maximum registration term in years times 12, less those whole months, less one more month where the expiry date does not fall on the same day of the month as the day of the order, divided by 12 and rounded down to a whole number. Where the restore-day years come to zero, no extension is billed.

Restore-day years are priced only after the domain's status reads active again and a restore charge dated the day of the order stands on it, the years being counted from the expiry date the restore leaves.

*Hypothetical, with a maximum registration term of 10 years:* order on 14 February 2029, expiry date on record 3 September 2030. The whole months come to 18; the expiry falls on another day of the month, so one more month is taken off: 120 less 18 less 1 leaves 101 months, which divided by 12 and rounded down gives 8 years. Had the expiry date been 14 February 2030, the 12 whole months and the same day of the month would give 108 months, so 9 years.

## B. Amount

The amount of a restore-day extension is the restore-day renewal component, less the restore-day credits, plus the TLD's ICANN fee for each of the restore-day years.

- The restore-day renewal component is the TLD's renewal price times the restore-day years, reduced by the percentage discount that applies to the order, rounded half up to the cent; the ICANN fee is never discounted.
- The restore-day credits are the amounts named as one of the restore-day credits, added together.
- The amount is worked out in this order: first the restore-day renewal component, then the restore-day credits are subtracted from it and that result is never taken below zero, and then the ICANN fee is added, every figure being in USD to the cent.

Where no percentage discount applies, the component is the renewal price times the restore-day years; where no restore-day credit applies, nothing is subtracted.

*Hypothetical prices (no real TLD): renewal USD 40.00, ICANN fee USD 0.30 a year, 3 restore-day years.*
1. No discount and no credit: component USD 120.00, plus ICANN fee USD 0.90, amount USD 120.90.
2. A hypothetical discount of 6 per cent: component USD 112.80; credits of USD 9.25 leave USD 103.55; plus USD 0.90, amount USD 104.45.
3. Credits of USD 125.00: the component less the credits is taken as zero; the ICANN fee of USD 0.90 is still added, amount USD 0.90.
